Answer: C
Reason: Comparing the two images reveals that the dense consolidation initially present in the left lung (Figure 1) has significantly resolved or cleared in the follow-up image (Figure 2), while new patchy opacities have appeared in the right upper lung. This radiographic pattern of resolving infiltrates in one location accompanied by new infiltrates in another is characteristic of migratory pulmonary opacities, supporting a diagnosis of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP).
